findings.failure_mode: An unavailable lease file aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error the caller can handle
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? instead of unwrap

findings.failure_mode: A malformed lease line with a non-numeric second field crashes the thread instead of yielding a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use result propagation (map_err) to return a typed parse error; change return type to Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: lossy as u16 cast discards high bits silently on values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value in range 65536..u32::MAX silently truncates to a wrong u16, corrupting lease data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed) and propagate the error via ? or map_err

findings.problem: split(\',\').collect() then parts[0] and parts[1] — allocates Vec and uses unchecked indexing
findings.failure_mode: Allocates a Vec for every line (wasteful), then parts[0] and parts[1] panic on lines with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields (e.g., empty lines or malformed entries)
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(\',\') to get name and value_str, handle None via ?, and avoid the Vec allocation entirely

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: Same as above: a line with zero commas panics at runtime
findings.fix: Eliminated by switching to split_once with proper None handling

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: A line with one or zero commas panics at runtime
findings.fix: Eliminated by switching to split_once with proper None handling

findings.problem: println! side effect inside data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: I/O is mixed into the core data pipeline, making the function non-deterministic and untestable without capturing stdout
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing path; logging belongs in the imperative shell layer that calls load_leases

findings.problem: load_leases returns Vec<Record> instead of Result — no way to propagate any of the above failures
findings.failure_mode: All errors must panic because the return type cannot carry failure information; the function cannot distinguish success from error at the call site
findings.fix: Change signature to fn load_leases(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LeaseError> where LeaseError is an enum covering I/O and parse variants

findings.problem: map(|part| part.trim().to_string()) allocates String for every field
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per field during parsing; small strings could be borrowed with &str from the line
findings.fix: Use split_once and trim to produce &str slices for name and value_str, then only allocate the final Record String for name

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() — unnecessary clone from already-owned String in Vec
findings.failure_mode: Redundant allocation; the String in the Vec is already owned
findings.fix: Eliminated by switch to split_once which yields &str directly, then use .to_string() only on the final name field
